description:
## Goal

Replace the current `(data, module)` pair stored per Transcript slot with a single struct, dispatched via an `OctoPi.TUI.Render` protocol. Drop the `Transcript.Entry` struct, drop the explicit `mod` arg from `Transcript.append/4`.

## Motivation

Today every Transcript entry carries two pieces of bookkeeping:

- `data` — canonical state (a binary for text/thinking blocks; a struct for everything else)
- `module` — pointer to a `Transcript.Renderer`-behaviour module, passed explicitly at `append/4` time

This was justified back when entry data could be anything (binaries, tuples, structs). After `.13` flattened the transcript and `.14` consolidated to spans, every live caller actually passes a struct. The `module` arg has become redundant — the struct already identifies the renderer kind.

Protocol dispatch on the entry struct collapses both fields into one. Drops `Entry`. Drops the explicit module arg. Replaces `function_exported?(mod, :span, 0)` reflection with a protocol callback.

## Design

### Protocol

```elixir
defprotocol OctoPi.TUI.Render do
  @fallback_to_any false

  def new(self, ctx)               # initialize state from canonical struct + ctx
  def put(self, snapshot)          # mid-stream update
  def finalize(self, snapshot)     # final state — to_lines runs once after this
  def to_lines(self)               # produce [String.t()] (no embedded \n)
  def span(self)                   # :open | :close | nil
  def wrap_span(self, lines, close_data | nil)  # only meaningful for :open
end
```

Each entry kind is a struct that holds **both** its canonical snapshot and any intermediate renderer state in one shape. The protocol impl mutates the struct in place across `new/put/finalize`. Example:

```elixir
defmodule OctoPi.TUI.Entry.Text do
  defstruct [:snapshot, :md_render]
end

defimpl OctoPi.TUI.Render, for: OctoPi.TUI.Entry.Text do
  def new(%Entry.Text{snapshot: s}, %{theme: t, width: w} = ctx) when not is_nil(t) and is_integer(w) do
    opts = ctx |> Map.drop([:theme, :width]) |> Enum.to_list()
    %Entry.Text{snapshot: s, md_render: MdRender.new(t, w, opts) |> MdRender.put(s)}
  end
  def new(e, _ctx), do: e   # deferred: ctx not yet known

  def put(%Entry.Text{md_render: nil} = e, s), do: %{e | snapshot: s}
  def put(%Entry.Text{md_render: r} = e, s), do: %{e | snapshot: s, md_render: MdRender.put(r, s)}

  def finalize(e, s) do
    e = put(e, s)
    case e.md_render do
      nil -> e
      r -> {_, r2} = MdRender.finalize(r); %{e | md_render: r2}
    end
  end

  def to_lines(%Entry.Text{md_render: nil}), do: []
  def to_lines(%Entry.Text{md_render: r}), do: MdRender.to_lines(r)

  def span(_), do: nil
  def wrap_span(_, lines, _), do: lines
end
```

### Default impls for non-span / wrapper-style entries

Provide a `use OctoPi.TUI.Render.Component` macro that synthesizes the trivial impl for any struct already implementing `OctoPi.TUI.Component`:

```elixir
defmodule OctoPi.TUI.Components.UserMessage do
  use OctoPi.TUI.Render.Component
  defstruct [...]
  ...
end
```

The macro generates:

```elixir
defimpl OctoPi.TUI.Render, for: __MODULE__ do
  def new(self, _ctx), do: self
  def put(self, _snap), do: self
  def finalize(self, _snap), do: self
  def to_lines(self), do: __MODULE__.render(self, ctx_width(self))   # via stored width
  def span(_), do: nil
  def wrap_span(_, lines, _), do: lines
end
```

Components that need width-at-render need a small adjustment — store `width` on the struct, set on `new(_, %{width: w})`. Same shape as the current `ComponentWrapper`.

### Transcript

```elixir
%Transcript{
  order:     [id, ...],          # newest-head, O(1) append
  streaming: %{id => struct},    # active state
  rendered:  %{id => [String.t()]},
  ctx:       term() | nil
}

@spec append(t(), id(), struct()) :: t()
def append(%__MODULE__{} = t, id, %_{} = entry) do
  %{t | order: [id | t.order],
        streaming: Map.put(t.streaming, id, Render.new(entry, t.ctx))}
end

@spec update(t(), id(), term()) :: t()
def update(%__MODULE__{} = t, id, snapshot) do
  state = Render.put(Map.fetch!(t.streaming, id), snapshot)
  %{t | streaming: Map.put(t.streaming, id, state)}
end

@spec finalize(t(), id(), term()) :: t()
def finalize(%__MODULE__{} = t, id, snapshot) do
  state = Render.finalize(Map.fetch!(t.streaming, id), snapshot)
  %{t | streaming: Map.delete(t.streaming, id),
        rendered:  Map.put(t.rendered, id, Render.to_lines(state))}
end
```

`compose/1` dispatches `Render.span/1` and `Render.wrap_span/3` instead of `mod.span()` / `mod.wrap_span(data, ...)`. The `data` arg threaded into spans becomes the entry struct itself — the same shape, since data and state are now one struct.

`Entry` struct deleted. `entries` map deleted. `fetch_module!/2` deleted (no module to fetch). `fetch_data!/2` becomes "fetch the current streaming state OR last finalized snapshot" — simplest is to keep a tiny `data: %{id => struct}` alongside `streaming` for finalized lookups, OR look up via `streaming[id] || ...rendered_snapshot...`. Decide during implementation based on caller needs (`Interactive.maybe_update_header_tool_flag` is the one tricky caller).

## Migration plan

1. **Define `OctoPi.TUI.Render` protocol** with the six callbacks. Add `Render.Component` `using` macro for the wrapper case.
2. **Migrate the four span-aware structs.** `AssistantHeader`, `AssistantStatus` already are structs — convert their existing `Renderer` behaviour impl into `defimpl Render` blocks. Same logic, different surface.
3. **Introduce `Entry.Text` and `Entry.Thinking` structs** wrapping the binary snapshot + intermediate state (the existing `MdRender` / italic-wrap state). `defimpl Render` for each.
4. **Migrate component wrappers.** `UserMessage`, `ToolExecution`, `BashExecution`, `CompactionSummaryMessage`, `Diff`. Each gets `use OctoPi.TUI.Render.Component`. Add `:width` field where needed.
5. **Rewrite `Transcript`.** Drop `Entry`, drop `entries` map, drop `module` arg from `append/4`. Compose dispatches via protocol.
6. **Update `Interactive`** callsites: `Transcript.append(t, k, snap, TextBlock)` → `Transcript.append(t, k, %Entry.Text{snapshot: snap})`. Same for thinking, header, status, csm, bash, tool, user.
7. **Update `AssistantMessage` component.** It builds a nested Transcript for blocks; same migration as Interactive.
8. **Tests.** Mechanical rename + struct wrapping.

## Acceptance

- `mix test` green (1286 / 0).
- `mix credo --strict` clean on all touched files.
- `mix format --check-formatted` clean.
- `mix dialyzer` no new warnings (current baseline: 3 pre-existing).
- `Transcript.Entry` module deleted. `Transcript.append/4` is now `Transcript.append/3` taking `(t, id, struct)`.
- No `function_exported?` calls in `Transcript`.
- Visual smoke test in tmux: streaming render unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Any change to OSC injection semantics (already correct from `.14`).
- Performance work beyond what falls out of the simplification.
- Persisting transcripts (the data/state merger makes serialization slightly weirder; address if/when needed).
title: Render protocol: drop Entry, dispatch on entry struct
